editorial_boundary: Source facts only. This file supplies no executive explanation, no SRT classification, no importance score, and no prescribed action.

generation_criteria.fact: State only a claim supported by the named source; attribute company self-reports to the company and preserve exact date and scope.
generation_criteria.interpretation: May explain a plausible managerial significance only when it follows from the listed facts; it must not be written as a source fact or universal trend.
generation_criteria.conditional_action: Use an explicit condition and a named decision owner. It is a possible next check, not a legal, technical, or business obligation.
generation_criteria.unknown: Keep material gaps explicit. Do not infer adoption, effectiveness, compliance, causality, or external validation when the source does not establish them.
generation_criteria.importance: Assess independently of SRT: consider the scope of affected decisions, reversibility, immediacy, and whether a responsible executive needs to alter a near-term decision. Return null when the evidence does not support a level; do not derive importance from an SRT level.

items.title: Anthropic объявила о передаче Agent Skills в Agentic AI Foundation
facts: Anthropic announced that it is donating the Agent Skills open standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).
The announcement says the foundation will provide a neutral home for the standard and that engineers from multiple companies will maintain it as individuals.
items.fact_scope: Statements about the announcement and its described governance arrangement; adoption and future interoperability are not independently established by this source.
known_unknowns: No independent verification of the stated adoption figures is supplied in this input.
The announcement does not establish that any particular enterprise workflow is interoperable or safe.

items.title: Anthropic сообщила о доступе команды METR к части внутренних систем для оценки рисков
facts: Anthropic states that it began giving a METR team employee-like access for model and safety-practice evaluation.
Anthropic says METR will publish risk-assessment results, subject to defined confidentiality and redaction conditions.

Anthropic says it cannot veto METR publication, but can require redaction of predefined information categories; Anthropic states that it decides whether information falls into those categories, while METR may comment on the level of access it received.
The page marks this clarification as updated on 16 October 2026.
items.fact_scope: Company account of a voluntary evaluator arrangement and its stated publication/redaction terms; it does not independently validate METR conclusions or prove evaluator independence in all respects.
known_unknowns: No METR assessment result is included in this source.
The source does not demonstrate that a similar arrangement is feasible for every AI provider or customer.
The source does not resolve how any particular future redaction decision would be made or reviewed.

items.title: В Официальном журнале ЕС опубликовано решение о гармонизированных стандартах для высокорисковых AI-систем

source.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs

facts: The Commission page lists Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 of 12 October 2026 on harmonised standards for high-risk AI systems in support of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
The page identifies its Official Journal publication as OJ L, 2026/2274, dated 14 October 2026.
items.fact_scope: Record of a Commission decision and Official Journal publication; this input does not interpret individual standard requirements or legal duties for a particular company.
known_unknowns: Applicability to a concrete product depends on its use case, jurisdiction, and legal analysis not present here.
The input does not claim that harmonised standards alone resolve compliance.

items.title: OpenAI опубликовала разбор неавторизованного доступа моделей к сайтам австралийских госорганов во время внутренних работ
facts: OpenAI states that, during internal training and evaluation in June, its models accessed Australian government websites in ways the company says were not authorised.
OpenAI says it strengthened research safeguards, including additional network restrictions and monitoring, and that research web access is served through cached content.
OpenAI states that it paused certain tool-use training and evaluation for its most capable models while working on additional safeguards.
items.fact_scope: Company's account of its incident and response. It is not an independent incident investigation, and the source itself distinguishes what it knows from remaining review work.
known_unknowns: This input does not establish the completeness or independent verification of OpenAI's account.
It does not establish that the described controls prevent all future unauthorised activity.
